summary.business_type: Professional / local service — Indian corporate compliance services firm (single Chennai office, Tamil Nadu-wide service area)
top_findings: No canonical tags on any of the 101 pages — high duplicate-content risk across ~85 near-identical service pages
Every non-home page title is duplicated: "... | FirstMan | FirstMan" (metadata template bug, ~99 pages)
No phone number anywhere on the site — no tel: links, not in header/footer/contact, not in schema
Government-fee amounts are null/missing in both page copy and Offer schema — the exact fact cost-intent searchers want
Organization schema uses a bare address string and generic type instead of ProfessionalService + PostalAddress + contactPoint
Topically related pages barely link to each other — e.g. the ISO Certification pillar page links to none of its 8 variant pages
No E-E-A-T signals anywhere: no named/credentialed authors, no testimonials, no case studies
quick_wins: Fix the title-template double-suffix bug in the shared Next.js metadata layout — one fix covers ~99 pages
Add a self-referencing canonical tag in the same shared metadata generator — one fix covers all 101 URLs
Add a phone number (tel: link) to the header/footer and contactPoint to schema
Add government-fee breakdown to the price block + Offer schema on service pages
Add reciprocal internal links: ISO pillar → its 8 variants, compliance spokes → the pillar guide
Add a CTA button to the /pricing page hero (currently has none)

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Correct robots.txt (only internal CRM app paths disallowed, marketing site fully open)
Valid sitemap.xml, 1:1 parity with actual site structure (81/81 service pages, 3/3 compare, 10/10 resources), no orphans, no dead entries
Clean single-hop redirects, real 404s, consistent security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) including on error pages
Server-rendered HTML throughout, no SPA shell, no JS wall for crawlers
Single H1 per page, viewport meta present everywhere

findings.title: No canonical tag on any page (site-wide)
findings.description: All 15 sampled pages across every template (homepage, service detail, resources, compare, pricing) render with no <link rel="canonical">. With ~85 near-identical /services/<slug> pages sharing one template, there is no self-referencing canonical to anchor Google's indexing decisions.
findings.recommendation: Add a self-referencing canonical URL to the shared Next.js metadata generator used across (marketing) route group templates — one fix covers all 101 URLs.

findings.title: Duplicated title tag suffix: "... | FirstMan | FirstMan"
findings.description: Verified on ~99 of 101 URLs (e.g. "DSC Class III - Sign & Encryption — Fees, documents & process | FirstMan | FirstMan", 86 chars). The page-level title already includes "| FirstMan" and the root layout's title template appends "| FirstMan" again.
findings.recommendation: Fix the metadata title template layering — either strip the per-page "| FirstMan" suffix or change the root layout's template to not re-append it. Single fix in the shared metadata layout.

findings.title: No Open Graph / Twitter Card tags anywhere
findings.description: No og:title/og:image/twitter:card tags found on any sampled page — hurts link-preview quality on WhatsApp and LinkedIn, both important channels for an India-based B2B services referral business.
findings.recommendation: Add OG/Twitter tags to the shared layout metadata, reusing the existing /brand/firstman-logo.png as the default og:image.

findings.title: No BreadcrumbList schema despite deep hierarchy
findings.description: ~90 pages sit under /services/, /resources/, /compare/ with no BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, losing a low-effort SERP enhancement and a clear hierarchy signal.
findings.recommendation: Add one BreadcrumbList component reused across the three route groups, deriving labels from existing route params/catalog data.

findings.title: Minor: /services hub only links 81 of 85 detail pages; other low-severity items
findings.description: 4 service pages are reachable only via sitemap/direct URL, not the hub page (orphan risk). Also: a 2-hop redirect on the http://www variant, X-Powered-By: Next.js disclosed on every response, no Permissions-Policy header.
findings.recommendation: Audit the /services hub's catalog query for the 4 missing entries; collapse the www redirect to one hop; strip X-Powered-By; add a Permissions-Policy header alongside the existing CSP/HSTS.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: /compare/<slug> pages lead with a genuine synthesized recommendation, not a bare comparison table
Resource articles carry real, visible publish/update dates
Service pages carry specific, citable cost/turnaround facts in their FAQ blocks

findings.title: Verbatim boilerplate reuse across unrelated services
findings.description: /services/dsc-class-iii-individual and /services/iso-27001-2013-certification open with identical sentences except for the service name; FSSAI, IEC, and trademark pages share an identical "What you receive" bullet block. Strong evidence the ~85 service pages are minimally differentiated beyond string substitution on one shared template.
findings.recommendation: Add a data-driven unique-content block (150-200 words) per service page, generated from the existing checklistTemplate/requiredDocuments catalog fields already stored per service — turns near-duplicate pages into genuinely differentiated ones without manual per-page writing.

findings.title: No E-E-A-T signals on any sampled page
findings.description: No named author with credentials, no testimonials, no case studies anywhere. Resource articles only carry a generic "FirstMan Team" byline. This matters more than average for a compliance/legal-adjacent business where trust directly drives conversion.
findings.recommendation: Add named practitioner bylines with credentials (CA/CS) to resource articles and flagship service pages; add client testimonials/case studies to the homepage and top-converting service pages.

findings.title: No freshness signal on service pages
findings.description: Service pages all resolve to an identical 2026-01-01 date (a deploy-time artifact, not real content freshness), with no visible "last reviewed" date — unlike resource articles, which do show real dates.
findings.recommendation: Surface a real "Last reviewed: [date]" on service pages tied to an actual review cadence, sourced from a genuine content-update timestamp rather than deploy time.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Consistent template structure and heading hierarchy across each page family
Existing internal navigation (header, footer, breadcrumb-style category links) does connect every page at a basic level

findings.title: Internal linking between topically related pages is largely absent
findings.description: Content-cluster analysis of 5 major topic groups (Company Formation, Annual Compliance, GST, ISO Certification, Tax Filing) found the ISO Certification pillar page (/services/iso-certification) links to NONE of its 8 certification variant pages, and none of the variants link to each other or back to the pillar — the single worst gap on the site. Annual Compliance is one-directional only (the pillar guide links down to 3 service pages, but none of them link back). GST and Tax Filing clusters have zero interlinking and no pillar page at all.
findings.recommendation: Add an "ISO standards" grid on /services/iso-certification linking all 8 variants (highest-leverage single fix on the site). Clone the reciprocal-linking module already built on /resources/annual-compliance-guide onto its service-page spokes. Build simple pillar sections for the GST and Tax Filing clusters.

findings.title: Title tag and canonical issues are fundamentally on-page defects
findings.description: The duplicated-title-suffix bug and site-wide missing canonicals (detailed under Technical SEO) are on-page metadata defects that directly determine what appears in search results and how duplicate near-identical pages get consolidated.
findings.recommendation: See Technical SEO fixes — same shared metadata layout, same two fixes, cross-referenced here because they are the most consequential on-page issues found.

findings.title: Compare pages never cross-link each other despite overlapping entities
findings.description: The 3 /compare/<slug> pages (private-limited-vs-llp, llp-vs-opc, proprietorship-vs-private-limited) never link to each other even though LLP appears in 2 of 3, and none link to /resources/how-to-choose-a-business-structure, the natural pillar for this cluster.
findings.recommendation: Add a small "Related comparisons" module cross-linking the 3 compare pages and the business-structure resource guide.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: Service + Offer schema with live INR pricing already implemented on all ~85 service pages, generated server-side from the catalog DB
Article schema with real dates on the 10 resource guides
FAQPage schema present on service and compare pages
All JSON-LD blocks are syntactically valid

findings.title: Organization address is a bare string, not a PostalAddress object (sitewide)
findings.description: The one shared Organization JSON-LD block (injected in the marketing layout, present on all ~101 pages) emits "address": "W-426A, Second Floor, ..." as a plain string instead of a structured PostalAddress object — this alone disqualifies the site from any Local Business rich-result eligibility. Because it's emitted from one shared component, the fix propagates everywhere at once.
findings.recommendation: Change address to a proper schema.org PostalAddress object (streetAddress, addressLocality, addressRegion, postalCode, addressCountry) in the shared JSON-LD-emitting component.

findings.title: Organization schema type should be ProfessionalService, not generic Organization
findings.description: Given the real single-location Chennai office and the professional-services nature of the business, @type should be ProfessionalService (or a more specific subtype) rather than generic Organization.
findings.recommendation: Change @type to ProfessionalService in the same shared component; add geo coordinates and openingHoursSpecification if available.

findings.title: No contactPoint / telephone in schema
findings.description: No contactPoint block exists in the Organization schema, and /contact itself has no visible tel:/mailto: link in the rendered HTML (cross-confirmed by the Local SEO audit).
findings.recommendation: Add a contactPoint with telephone once a phone number is added to the site (see Local SEO finding) — same shared component fix.

findings.title: No BreadcrumbList schema anywhere
findings.description: Despite the deep /services/, /resources/, /compare/ hierarchy, no page emits BreadcrumbList JSON-LD.
findings.recommendation: Add one reusable BreadcrumbList component across the three route groups (see Technical SEO — same fix, cross-referenced).

findings.title: Article schema missing image and publisher
findings.description: The 10 resource-guide Article blocks omit `image` (a property Google lists as required for Article rich-result eligibility) and `publisher`.
findings.recommendation: Add image and publisher (referencing the Organization block) to the existing Article generator used for /resources/<slug> pages; reuse the same generator for /compare/<slug> pages, which currently carry only FAQPage schema with no Article/WebPage description of the comparison itself.

findings.title: No page-specific schema on /pricing, /about, /services hub
findings.description: These pages currently rely solely on the sitewide Organization block with no page-specific structured data.
findings.recommendation: Low priority — add WebPage/ItemList schema opportunistically if revisiting these templates for other reasons.

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: Full static/ISR caching confirmed (Cache-Control: s-maxage=31536000, X-Nextjs-Cache: HIT)
Fonts self-hosted via next/font with font-display: swap
Images used via next/image with explicit dimensions — zero CLS risk from images
All JS chunks load async/non-blocking; recently-added GA/GTM correctly uses strategy="afterInteractive" rather than blocking hydration

findings.title: 114KB render-blocking global CSS bundle, not split per route
findings.description: The same global Tailwind CSS bundle (114.6KB) loads on every page regardless of what that page actually uses — unusually large for a JIT-purged Tailwind 4 build, and directly gates LCP since it's render-blocking.
findings.recommendation: Audit the Tailwind content globs and any dynamically-constructed class names (which defeat purging) to shrink the shared CSS bundle.

findings.title: 177KB oversized shared JS chunk loaded on every route
findings.description: One shared JS chunk (177KB) is the largest of ~15-20 chunks by far and loads even on lightweight pages like /pricing that don't need most of it.
findings.recommendation: Route-split this chunk so static/simple pages don't pay its full cost.

findings.title: CWV estimates sit close to the pass/fail edge on mobile (lab-only data, no CrUX access)
findings.description: Homepage ~1.9-2.3s LCP / ~120-220ms INP proxy / ~0.01-0.03 CLS; service and pricing pages estimated similarly, all passing but close enough to the ceiling that real mid-tier-Android/4G field data could tip them into "needs improvement." This can't be confirmed without CrUX/PSI API access, which isn't configured in this environment.
findings.recommendation: Connect Google PageSpeed Insights / CrUX API credentials to replace these lab estimates with real field data (see Phase 4).

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: robots.txt fully open to AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot etc.), no AI-specific blocks
/llms.txt present and well-formed
All pages server-rendered, no JS wall blocking AI crawlers
Resource articles consistently open with a self-contained direct-answer sentence in the first ~40 words
/compare/* pages combine literal comparison tables with question-form FAQs — the best-optimized content type on the site for AI extraction
Visible and machine-detected publication/update dates on resource articles

findings.title: Resource guides and compare pages likely under-use FAQPage/Article schema for AI extraction
findings.description: The GEO-focused audit pass found genuine, well-formed Q&A content on resource guides and compare pages (question-form headers, single-paragraph answers) but reported it couldn't confirm matching JSON-LD there. Note: this appears to partially conflict with the Schema audit's finding that FAQPage schema IS present on service/compare page templates — the discrepancy likely reflects the resource-guide template specifically lacking FAQPage/Article-with-full-properties rather than a sitewide absence. Treat as: resource guides (/resources/<slug>) are the template most likely to be under-schema'd; verify directly before treating either finding as final.
findings.recommendation: Add FAQPage JSON-LD to the 10 /resources/<slug> guides from their existing visible Q&A content, and complete their Article schema (image, publisher — see Schema section) — regardless of which audit pass is more precise, this is a low-effort, high-impact fix.

findings.title: Generic team byline, no named/credentialed author
findings.description: Every resource article credits "By FirstMan Corporate Services Team" rather than a named individual with CA/CS credentials — weakens the authority signal AI systems weigh when selecting sources on compliance/legal topics.
findings.recommendation: Same fix as the Content Quality E-E-A-T finding — add named, credentialed bylines.

findings.title: Organization schema too thin for strong brand/entity grounding
findings.description: Same underlying issue as the Schema section — bare address string, generic Organization type, no contactPoint reduces how confidently AI systems can ground "FirstMan Corporate Services" as a verified real-world entity.
findings.recommendation: Same fix as Schema section — ProfessionalService + PostalAddress + contactPoint.

findings.title: llms.txt appears to list only /services/* pages, not resources/compare
findings.description: The reviewed portion of /llms.txt did not include the resource guides or compare pages, which are actually the site's strongest citable content per this audit.
findings.recommendation: Low priority per current AI-engine behavior (llms.txt has limited confirmed uptake) — expand opportunistically, don't over-invest.

categories.name: Images
what_works: The marketing site is deliberately icon-driven (lucide-react SVG icons) rather than photo-heavy, so there is very little raster-image surface area to get wrong
The one raster image found (the logo, src/components/marketing/logo.tsx) uses next/image correctly: descriptive alt text, explicit width/height, and priority loading
No tags anywhere on the marketing site outside next/image, and no missing-alt risk found in the codebase

findings.title: Missed opportunity for trust-building photography
findings.description: The near-total absence of real photography (office, team, client-facing imagery) is technically clean but ties into the E-E-A-T/trust gap flagged under Content Quality and Local SEO — a compliance-services firm often benefits from showing a real office and real people.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding a small set of real photos (office exterior/interior, team) alongside the E-E-A-T improvements in Phase 3 — content strategy, not a technical image-SEO fix.

supplementary_categories.name: Local SEO
supplementary_categories.note: Not part of the 7 officially-weighted categories, but material for this business type (single physical location, geographically bounded service area). Weighted informally into the On-Page/Schema commentary above where findings overlap.
what_works: Address is 100% consistent across JSON-LD, footer, and /contact body text on every page checked
GSTIN + LLPIN displayed sitewide and match schema — a strong, vertical-appropriate trust signal for a compliance-services firm

findings.title: No phone number anywhere on the site
findings.description: Zero tel: links and zero phone number patterns found across the full rendered HTML of /, /about, /contact. The only "phone"-labeled field is the visitor's own number in the enquiry form. No telephone/contactPoint in schema either.
findings.recommendation: Add a real phone number to the header/footer and /contact page as a tel: link, plus contactPoint.telephone in the Organization schema.

findings.title: No Chennai/Tamil Nadu-specific landing content
findings.description: All ~85 service pages use identical generic titles ("<Service> — Fees, documents & process"); "Tamil Nadu"/"Chennai" appear only in the shared footer/JSON-LD, never in page-specific H1s or titles, despite areaServed: "Tamil Nadu" in schema.
findings.recommendation: Add Chennai/Tamil Nadu qualifiers to titles/H1s of the top-converting service pages (company registration, GST, compliance) — dedicated local-intent pages are a top local-organic ranking factor.

findings.title: No Maps embed or directions link on /contact
findings.description: The only iframe found on /contact is Google Tag Manager's noscript tag — no embedded map or "Get Directions" link.
findings.recommendation: Embed a Google Maps iframe and add a directions link on /contact.

findings.title: No testimonials or review schema
findings.description: No client testimonials or Review/AggregateRating schema found anywhere on the site.
findings.recommendation: Same fix as the Content Quality E-E-A-T recommendation — add testimonials, consider review schema once genuine reviews exist.

findings.title: GBP listing status and citation presence unverifiable from the site alone
findings.description: Google Business Profile status/category/reviews, Tier-1 citation presence (JustDial/Sulekha/etc.), and proximity-based local-pack ranking require Maps/GBP or search-API access not available in this environment — explicitly flagged as unverified, not assumed absent.
findings.recommendation: Business owner should independently confirm/claim/optimize the GBP listing; revisit with Maps API access if it becomes available.

supplementary_categories.name: Search Experience (SXO)
supplementary_categories.note: Page-type-mismatch and persona-scoring analysis against 4 representative target queries.

findings.title: Government-fee transparency missing site-wide
findings.description: govtFeePaise is null in Offer schema on all 3 sampled service pages, and the same gap shows in page copy — this is literally the fact that cost-intent queries ("trademark registration India cost") are searching for. Competing SERP results for this query show explicit fee breakdowns (e.g. ₹4,500 individual/MSME vs ₹9,000 company).
findings.recommendation: Add a government-fee line item (varying by applicant type where applicable) to the price block and Offer schema on every service page — the single highest-leverage fix identified across the entire audit for conversion + informational-query matching.

findings.title: One generic template serves both transactional and informational search intent
findings.description: The same ~380-word service-page template with an identical 4-question FAQ (included? / cost? / how long? / track progress?) is used regardless of whether the target query is transactional ("register a company") or informational ("GST registration process") — competing content for informational queries runs 1,500-3,000 words with step-by-step guidance.
findings.recommendation: Add 2-3 query-specific FAQ entries per service (eligibility, minimum capital, individual-vs-company fee) on top of the existing generic 4, and route deeper informational intent to the /resources hub rather than trying to serve it entirely from the thin service-page template.

findings.title: Compliance-checklist content fragmented across 3 separate pages
findings.description: The "annual compliance checklist" resource page omits due dates and penalties, forcing 2 extra clicks to /resources/annual-compliance-calendar and /resources/penalties-for-missing-compliance-deadlines — while competing long-form articles cover due dates + penalties in one piece.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate due-date and penalty data directly into the compliance-checklist article, or clearly cross-link all 3 pieces to each other.

supplementary_categories.name: Visual / UX
supplementary_categories.note: Screenshots captured live via Playwright (desktop + mobile) for homepage, a service detail page, and /pricing.
what_works: Strong homepage above-the-fold clarity on both viewports — value prop, primary/secondary CTA, and trust badges all visible with no scroll
Genuine price transparency (real ₹ figures, not "contact us")
Footer displays GSTIN/LLPIN/registered address on every page — a strong compliance-firm trust signal
Pricing table degrades gracefully to stacked cards on mobile with no horizontal overflow
No layout bugs or overlaps found anywhere sampled

findings.title: Pricing page hero has no CTA button
findings.description: The /pricing hero shows only a headline/subhead with no CTA — the only conversion path on this very long (80+ service row) page is scrolling all the way down or using the sticky header button.
findings.recommendation: Add a CTA button directly in the pricing page hero.

findings.title: Mobile header hides the primary CTA and login behind a hamburger menu
findings.description: The desktop "Talk to an expert" CTA and "Client login" link disappear entirely on mobile, leaving only a hamburger icon — the primary conversion action is one extra tap away on every page.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent visible contact action (call icon or sticky bar) to the mobile header instead of hiding it in the hamburger menu.

findings.title: Service-detail CTA sits just below the mobile fold
findings.description: Headline, description, and price are visible without scrolling on mobile, but the enquiry form/CTA itself needs one scroll.
findings.recommendation: Consider tightening the mobile hero to bring the CTA into the initial viewport, or add a sticky mobile CTA bar.

supplementary_categories.name: Sitemap
supplementary_categories.note: Folded into the Technical SEO narrative above; scored separately here for detail.

findings.title: Two live pages missing from the sitemap
findings.description: /legal/privacy and /legal/terms both return 200 and are linked from the homepage footer, but neither appears in sitemap.xml, and neither is disallowed in robots.txt.
findings.recommendation: Add both to the sitemap generator's route enumeration.

findings.title: All 101 lastmod values are identical
findings.description: Every URL shares the exact same lastmod timestamp — clearly a build/render-time stamp rather than a real content-change date, providing zero recrawl-priority signal.
findings.recommendation: Drive lastmod from a real content-updated timestamp per page, touched only when content actually changes, or omit the field entirely.

supplementary_categories.name: Backlinks
supplementary_categories.note: Data-insufficient placeholder, not a real health score — domain is not yet present in Common Crawl (the only backlink data source available in this environment; no Moz/Bing/DataForSEO API keys configured). Expected for a newly launched marketing site, not a tool failure or a confirmed "zero backlinks" finding.

findings.title: No backlink data source has any record of the domain
findings.description: Common Crawl reports in_crawl: false / in_rankings: false for firstmancorp.com. This is a coverage gap (CC is a sampled, quarterly-refreshed graph that under-represents small/new/regional sites), not evidence the profile is empty.
findings.recommendation: Connect Google Search Console (free, direct-from-Google Links report) and add a free Moz API key to close the data gap; re-check Common Crawl in ~3 months at its next quarterly refresh.

findings.title: Realistic regional link-building opportunities
findings.description: Consistent with a brand-new regional professional-services site with no digital-PR history — framed as an opportunity, not a defect.
findings.recommendation: Pursue Justdial/Sulekha/IndiaMART/Google Business Profile listings, Madras/Tamil Nadu Chamber of Commerce membership listings, guest articles on Indian business/finance outlets (Inc42, YourStory) on GST/MSME/trademark topics, and referral links from partner CA/CS/legal firms.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Fix the duplicated title-tag suffix bug ("| FirstMan | FirstMan") in the shared Next.js metadata layout — covers ~99 pages in one fix
Add self-referencing canonical tags in the same shared metadata generator — covers all 101 URLs
Add a real phone number as a tel: link to the header/footer and /contact page, plus contactPoint.telephone in schema
Add government-fee amounts to the price block and Offer schema on every service page

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Upgrade the shared Organization JSON-LD to ProfessionalService with a structured PostalAddress object and contactPoint
Add a reusable BreadcrumbList component across the /services, /resources, /compare route groups
Add OG/Twitter Card tags to the shared layout metadata, reusing the existing brand logo

Fix the worst internal-linking gaps: link /services/iso-certification to all 8 of its variant pages; add reciprocal links from Annual Compliance service pages back to their pillar guide; cross-link the 3 /compare pages
Add a data-driven unique-content block per service page sourced from existing checklistTemplate/requiredDocuments catalog fields
Add a CTA button to the /pricing hero; surface a persistent mobile CTA instead of hiding it behind the hamburger menu

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Add named, credentialed (CA/CS) bylines to resource articles and flagship service pages
Add client testimonials/case studies to the homepage and top-converting service pages; consider Review schema once genuine reviews exist
Add Chennai/Tamil Nadu-specific qualifiers to titles/H1s of top-converting service pages
Embed a Google Maps iframe and directions link on /contact
Consolidate the compliance-checklist content currently fragmented across 3 pages
Add FAQPage + complete Article schema (image, publisher) to the 10 /resources/<slug> guides
Add the 2 missing legal pages to the sitemap; fix the uniform lastmod timestamp
Reduce the shared CSS (114KB) and JS chunk (177KB) sizes for lighter page weight sitewide

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Connect Google Search Console + PageSpeed Insights/CrUX API credentials to replace lab-only performance estimates with real field data
Add a free Moz API key; monitor for Common Crawl re-inclusion at its next quarterly refresh
Pursue realistic regional link-building: GBP listing, JustDial/Sulekha/IndiaMART, Chamber of Commerce, guest posts on Indian business/finance outlets, partner CA/CS referral links
Capture an SEO drift baseline now so future changes can be compared against this audit
Re-audit after Phase 1-2 ships to confirm the canonical/title/schema fixes landed correctly and measure score improvement
